references.text: Basic command regarding the Feast of Unleavened Bread, where the Israelites are to eat unleavened bread for seven days in remembrance of the exodus from Egypt.
Moses exhorts the people to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the month of Abib, when they came out of Egypt.
Parallel command to observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days in the month of Abib.
Detailed regulations concerning the Feast of Unleavened Bread in Leviticus.
Sacrificial laws associated with the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
Command to keep Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the month of Abib in remembrance of the exodus from Egypt.
The three annual feasts where all men must appear before the Lord, and none shall come empty-handed.
King Hezekiah's celebration of the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.
Josiah's celebration of Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
The Israelites celebrate the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days with joy after returning from exile.
The first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, when the disciples prepared the Passover meal for Jesus.
Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread as the context for the story of Jesus' suffering.
The Feast of Unleavened Bread, also called Passover, was approaching.
Peter's arrest during the days of Unleavened Bread.
Paul travels after the days of Unleavened Bread.
Paul uses the symbolism of the Feast of Unleavened Bread and the Passover lamb as a picture of Christ and the Christian life.
Deuteronomy expands on the theological motivation behind the command by calling the bread 'the bread of affliction' and emphasizing the memory of the flight from Egypt.
This verse emphasizes that it is God himself who brought the people out, and establishes the feast as a permanent ordinance for all generations.
Leviticus 23 integrates the feast into the fixed festival calendar by specifying the dates, while the source verse focuses on the historical reason.
This verse completes the picture by specifying that the seventh day is a day of rest and a sacred assembly without work.
This verse expands on the requirements by emphasizing that no leavened bread may be found throughout the land during the entire festival period.
This verse elaborates on the consequences by stating that leaven must be removed from the first day and that breaking the rule leads to being cut off.
